_about: Approved-decision database for interaction contracts (canvas tools and portal subtypes). One entry per contract x dimension. Agents seed future volatile matrices from here: an approved decision that maps onto a new contract (same archetype / object class / portal class) is re-proposed with high confidence. Only verdict:'approved' rows count as precedent; 'proposed' rows are awaiting user confirmation in the volatile canvas. Schema: tools.<name>.family = tool|portal, and tools.<name>.decisions.<D##> = { behavior, source: stated|research|pattern|guess|precedent, confidence: 0-100, verdict: proposed|approved|rejected, decided: date|null }. Each contract answers exactly the dimensions DIMENSIONS.md scopes to its family; `cargo xtask contracts` enforces the parity between this file, the registry, and the contract markdown. Append-only in spirit: superseded decisions are overwritten only by a newer user approval.

D01.behavior: Dock Text icon opens a flyout submenu: (1) Text box · (2) Sticky note. Selecting a row arms that variant with a cursor-locked ghost. Hotkeys: T → Text box, N → Sticky. Palette: text / sticky (+ aliases). Space/Enter re-arms the last of the two (P0.4/P0.7).

D02.behavior: Text box: one-shot — after place+edit-blur (or Esc commit), return to Select. Sticky: stays armed after commit; Tab / Shift+Tab while editing spawns an adjacent sticky and keeps the tool armed. Esc while armed (no edit) disarms to Select.

D03.behavior: Armed → GhostFollow (default-size ghost locked to cursor) → Press → (ClickPlace | DragScale) → Commit → enter inline edit. Click-release places at default world size. Press-drag-release places and scales. Replaces P2.PlaceOnce for text/sticky (new L2: GhostPlace).

D04.behavior: Cursor travel > draft.drag_threshold (4 screen px) before release = DragScale; release within threshold = ClickPlace at default size. Drag under MIN_DRAW discards.

D05.behavior: Held Shift during DragScale locks aspect: Sticky → square; Text box → lock to default aspect (280×48). No Alt/Ctrl create modifiers in v1.

D06.behavior: F9 grid snap applies to the ghost's anchor (Text: top-left of default rect; Sticky: center) and to both corners of a DragScale rect. F8 ortho does not apply to area placement. Object-snap off for v1.

D07.behavior: n/a during placement (no Tab direction lock). Tab while editing a sticky is the spawn-adjacent command (D02), not a place-time lock.

D08.behavior: No digit-entry sizing during place (Art. III). After commit, font size / box size edit via inspector + bbox grips only.

D09.behavior: While Armed: ghosted Text box or sticky preview locked to the cursor at the default world size (text: 280×48 + sample Text; sticky: STICKY_SIZE + yellow fill), alpha from place.ghost_alpha. During DragScale: live sized ghost. Paint always uses world metrics × camera zoom (font = size×z, wrap = rect.w×z) with no screen-constant / auto-fit path and no relative-scale floor.

D10.behavior: While Armed / DragScale the ghost is the cursor feedback (plus optional thin crosshair at the anchor). No system I-beam until inline edit starts after commit.

D11.behavior: Text box → TextNode (fill=None, default text Text, size 24 world). Sticky → TextNode with STICKY_FILL + STICKY_INK, empty text, size 24 world. Journal cmds board.tool.text / board.tool.sticky; one gesture = one undo. Immediately open inline edit. Creation DragScale sets rect from drag and scales font by mean scale vs default rect. Subsequent bbox resize of an existing node changes the frame only — authored font size stays put and text reflows.

D12.behavior: Esc while GhostFollow / mid-DragScale → disarm to Select, no node (P0.1). Esc while inline-editing → commit text + peel edit (sticky stays armed per D02; text returns to Select).

D13.behavior: Standard node resize bbox + rotation (P1.node). Multi-select uses the shared group bbox; group uniform scale also scales TextNode.size.

D14.behavior: Double-click enters inline edit. Inspector edits family / size / color / align / fill. Single-node bbox resize = frame-only reflow at fixed authored font size. No Miro Auto font size.

D15.behavior: Cut (Art. III): Miro Auto font size; sticky bulk-mode / spreadsheet paste; sticky stack; emoji reactions; S/M/L size picker chrome; screen-constant text / LOD that changes relative glyph size vs geometry.

D16.behavior: Next Text box / sticky consumes the last single-node Text edit when present: family, size, color, align; sticky also inherits fill (else STICKY_FILL). Defaults when none: Text box fill=None size 24; sticky yellow fill size 24.

D17.behavior: AABB of the text/sticky rect (area pick), including the fill for stickies. Marquee intersects the rect. Not stroke-precise.

D01.behavior: L key; palette: type 'line' + Enter; tools-rail icon; Space/Enter re-arms when Line was the last command (P0.4/P0.7).

D03.behavior: Armed -> FirstPoint -> SecondPoint -> Commit. Both grammars commit identically: click-move-click and press-drag-release (P2.RhinoDraft.gesture).

D04.behavior: Cursor travel > draft.drag_threshold (4 px) before release = drag grammar; otherwise click grammar.

D05.behavior: Held Shift inverts the F8 ortho state for the pending segment, 45-degree steps (P2.RhinoDraft.ortho).

D06.behavior: F8 ortho + F9 grid snap apply to both endpoints; endpoint object-snap to node edges/anchors within draft.osnap_radius.

D07.behavior: Tab locks the segment direction at its current angle; movement then only changes length; Tab again unlocks; Shift/ortho ignored while locked.

D08.behavior: After the first point, typed digits set length; Enter or the committing click places the end point at that distance along the current cursor direction. Backspace edits (P2.RhinoDraft.numeric).

D09.behavior: Rubber band from first point (constraint-resolved); dock readout shows live length + angle; numeric entry echoes next to the readout.

D10.behavior: Crosshair while armed; small lock glyph appended while Tab-locked.

D11.behavior: A parametric 2-point line node; stroke from P1.curve.create-style when the last single-node edit exists, else default_curve_stroke(fg) (Square end caps, Miter joins, 2 px); opacity from last edit or 1.0; journal cmd board.tool.line; one gesture = one undo (P0.2/P0.3).

D12.behavior: Esc during numeric entry clears the entry; next Esc removes the first point (back to Armed); next disarms to Select (P2.RhinoDraft.esc, P0.1).

D13.behavior: Endpoint grips only, no resize bbox (P1.curve.grips), single or multi-select. Homogeneous multi-line: grips on every line, no per-line outline, no group bbox handles. Grip drag moves that endpoint; ortho/snap apply.

D14.behavior: Grip drag re-journals as a point edit; Direct Selection (A) sees the same two anchors; Ctrl+J joins endpoints with other curves (P1.curve.style).

D15.behavior: Cut (Art. III): Rhino BothSides/Normal/Angled command options; length<angle typed syntax; chaining (that's the Polyline tool).

D16.behavior: Yes — last single-node edit seeds stroke + opacity (P1.curve.create-style); default stroke = default_curve_stroke(fg) (Square cap, 2 px) when none.

D17.behavior: Stroke-precise click + marquee (P1.curve.pick): hit_stroke + pick.slop (4 screen px); never the node AABB alone. Legacy ShapeKind::Line included.

portal-lens-repository.reference: GitKraken / GitLens commit graph, GitHub network graph, git log --graph

D01.behavior: Palette 'repository lens' + Enter (aliases: repo lens, git graph, history portal); tools-rail Portals flyout; command board.portal.repo_lens, board tabs only (P0.7/P0.8). No single-key chord in v1 (OQ3).

D02.behavior: One-shot: commit returns to Select; Space/Enter re-arms (P2.DragShape, P0.4).

D03.behavior: Armed -> Dragging(rect) -> Committed(unbound). Press-drag-release defines the frame; release commits an unbound portal painting a 'Choose repository...' empty state. Binding is a separate, non-modal step; no file dialog opens inside a draw gesture.

D04.behavior: Travel > draft.drag_threshold (4 px) = drag grammar (frame = dragged rect); below it, a portal.repo.default_size frame (960x540 world units) centred on the click, as board::place_frame_at already does for the Frame tool. Deviates P2.DragShape, which discards sub-MIN_DRAW releases.

D05.behavior: Shift during the drag locks 16:9; unmodified drags are free-aspect. Deviates the Frame tool's frame_drag_rect, which locks the preset aspect unconditionally, and P1.shape.aspect, whose Shift means square: the frame's width is how much history is on screen. Ctrl/Alt unassigned in v1.

D06.behavior: F9 grid snap and smart guides apply to the frame rect as for a Frame node (P1.node.move); F8 ortho is n/a for an axis-aligned rect. Contents never snap.

D07.behavior: n/a - no directional parameter in a rect placement.

D08.behavior: n/a in v1; typed frame dimensions are a non-goal (D15) rather than invented for one node kind.

D09.behavior: Drag: frame outline in Palette::portal + live w x h in the dock readout (line D09 precedent). Bound and idle: repository name, HEAD short ref, commits in window, as-of pin, health. Focused commit: short SHA, author, date, subject.

D10.behavior: Crosshair while armed; arrow over an unfocused portal; arrow inside a focused portal, PointingHand over a commit dot with an open action.

D11.behavior: One journaled Add of a portal node { rect, class: Generated, kind: RepoLens, source: None, query: RepoQuery::default() }. Frame, source, query journaled; contents never (Art. VI.3). One gesture = one undo. No style state consumed.

D12.behavior: Esc peels one layer per press (P0.1): contents focus -> drag draft -> armed tool -> selection. A focused portal registers the contents-focus layer for that frame only.

D13.behavior: Frame selects with standard frame handles, but portals participate in a future handle carousel shared with frames, rectangles, and wire-capable nodes: handles fade in near an edge; resize, wire creation, crop, and future edge actions stack at the same edge anchor; the primary action is centered, secondary actions slide aside with opacity/ease transitions and scroll into the primary slot as the cursor approaches them. Contents expose no grips and are not selectable. Resize re-lays-out rather than scaling; rotation rotates the painted result. The carousel ships in a later shared-handles pass.

D14.behavior: Re-edit through the Portal sidebar section (visible when a portal is selected) or the portal.repo.* commands; each edit is a journaled Patch of source/query, and contents regenerate from it.

D15.behavior: Cut (Art. III): staging, committing, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, stash, fetch, pull, push, branch/tag deletion, diff and blame, conflict resolution, issues and PR data, authenticated host APIs, per-file history, Gource-style playback, typed frame dimensions, and a portal-local minimap. Not cut: human-directed branch create, checkout, and merge are allowed only as explicit per-action write-back commands with journaled intent and named targets (Art. IX.5); they are never available to agents.

D16.behavior: No. The frame paints from Palette::portal and the portal token block; it neither consumes nor becomes BoardLastStyle. Deviates P1.shape.style so analysis surfaces stay identical across boards and both apps (Art. X).

D17.behavior: Frame picks on its rect. Contents become interactive only when focused and the portal apparent scale passes portal.repo.interact_zoom. Double-click or Enter focuses contents; a caption maximize button or border double-click within portal.repo.border_hit_px temporarily maximizes contents to the viewport. Focused/interactive commit dots and ribbons hit-test with pick.slop. Clicking outside, Esc, or leaving maximize drops contents focus.

D18.behavior: Generated. No journal owns mutations inside it: contents are a deterministic function of (object database, source, query, frame size) and are never journaled (Art. V.3, VI.3). Journaled acts are frame-only: place, move, resize, rebind, re-query, delete, bake.

D19.behavior: One SourceUri { kind: LocalFs } naming a git worktree or bare repository directory, relative-first (Art. IX.2). Bound by portal.repo.source (picker, empty-state button, sidebar) or by dropping a folder containing .git onto an unbound portal; rebinding is a journaled Patch that discards cached contents. Refused in v1: remote URLs and hosted APIs (Art. I.4).

D20.behavior: RepoQuery { refs (All|Heads|Named + include_remotes + hidden), window (Last(n)|Since(date)|Range(a..b)), as_of (None|Commit|Date), axis (Topological|Chronological, OQ1), trunk pinned to lane 0 (default remote HEAD branch, else main/master, else first ref by name), max_commits default 2000 with a visible 'N older commits not shown' band }.

D21.behavior: Recompute on bind, query patch, frame resize, portal.repo.refresh, and a debounced watch of HEAD/refs/packed-refs (1000 ms). Background thread, generation-tagged; stale results discarded (Art. II.3). While running, last good contents stay at stale_alpha (0.6) with a progress strip. A portal pinned by as_of never auto-refreshes past its pin and captions 'pinned'.

D22.behavior: Hover commit: tooltip (short SHA, author, date, subject, containing refs). Hover ref: reachable commits keep full alpha, rest dim to dim_alpha (0.25) - the Lens convention. Click: focus, details to the dock readout. Double-click a commit: open its web page when a configured remote matches a known host pattern, else inert (P0.8). Ctrl+C copies the full SHA. Esc clears focus. No board tool reaches the contents. The frame->contents coordinate map is defined and used by hit-testing now.

D23.behavior: LOD buckets key on world px per commit column. < portal.repo.lod_ribbon_px: ribbons + chevrons + ref tips, no dots. portal.repo.lod_ribbon_px..portal.repo.lod_detail_px: dots + ribbons + tags. >= portal.repo.lod_detail_px: dots plus short SHA, subject, author initials, date ticks. lod_ribbon_px and lod_detail_px are fine-tuning dashboard sliders. Ribbon meshes tessellate once per lane/zoom bucket and cache.

D24.behavior: slate-artifact emits the regenerated contents as SVG under the Art. IV.3 ceiling from the same layout function the painter uses, plus a provenance caption (repository, HEAD short SHA, as-of, ref set, commit count, generation time). No script, no fetch. An unbound or Missing portal exports its state card, not an empty rectangle.

D25.behavior: portal.repo.bake emits one journaled Add batch of authored nodes matching the current contents, grouped, with a provenance text node (Art. VI.3). The portal stays live: bake copies, it does not convert.

D26.behavior: Frame, source, and query sync as journal deltas. Contents are per-peer and never transmitted; each peer regenerates from its own clone. A peer that cannot resolve the locator paints Unknown naming the locator it tried (Art. IX.3). Focus, hover, and search are presence (Art. VIII.5).

D27.behavior: Every board.portal.repo_lens / portal.repo.* command is a registry SPEC and therefore MCP-reachable; frame/source/query mutations stage for acceptance. The beacon carries locator, HEAD, ref set, window, as_of, and focused commit. Humans may issue explicit write-back commands for branch create, checkout, and merge. Agents may never run git write/network commands, invoke write-back commands, or add commits, refs, or edges; agent-authored lane/epoch labels are deferred to the overlay pattern.

D28.behavior: Same object database + same query + same frame size => byte-identical layout. Commits sort by (commit_time, oid); lane assignment is one forward pass with first-parent inheritance and trunk pinned to lane 0; nothing reads the wall clock except generated_at, which is excluded from RepoGraph::fingerprint() (code-lens precedent). The fingerprint gates re-layout, the beacon write, and the determinism golden test.

D29.behavior: Background extraction over crossbeam-channel, generation-tagged, drained once per frame. Budget: 5000 commits extracted < 1 s, layout < 50 ms, paint windowed to the visible time range so a 100k-commit repository pans at 60 fps. Layout cached by (fingerprint, query, frame_size); meshes by (lane, zoom bucket). max_commits 2000 by default.

D30.behavior: Unbound; Unknown (initial/unresolved, neutral marker, not the missing marker); Analyzing (last good contents at stale_alpha + progress strip); Ready; Missing (locator named, last-known summary kept); NotARepository (names the folder); Unreadable(msg) (no partial graph presented as complete); Shallow(n) (.git/shallow detected, truncation marked); plus a Remotes(list) caption on every bound state so the fork surface being drawn is stated.

D31.behavior: Journaled: frame rect, rotation, source, and every query field including hidden refs and the as-of pin. Derived per-peer and never journaled or exported: focus, hover, tooltip, search, contents-focus mode, analysis status, cached layout, last-good contents.

D32.behavior: Nothing to consent to, and this is a property of the design rather than an omission: contents are extracted from a local repository directory the human picked, no code from that repository is ever executed, and remote URLs and hosted APIs are refused as source kinds (D19, Art. I.4). The portal opens no network connection, so no origin permission exists. Restated from already-approved D15/D19/D27 when D32 joined the registry.

portal-agent-link.reference: Cursor SDK sidecar + local agent file contract

D32.behavior: The agent runtime is out-of-process and user-run: Slate never spawns it (D15) and reaches it only through JSON files under the AI workspace the human established. Slate loads no page, script, or network endpoint on the portal's behalf, so there is no origin consent to grant - the trust boundary is the human's decision to run the sidecar, and staged proposals are the acceptance gate for everything it produces (D27, Art. VII.6).

edit-mode-drag.reference: Windows File Explorer drag / context menu

D01.behavior: Mode dock exposes View and Edit. Edit arms real filesystem operations for the active tab only; View refuses them.

D02.behavior: Mode persists while the tab is active or parked, but fresh roots and launches reset to View. Drag operations are one-shot.

D03.behavior: Edit mode: LMB down on file/folder, drag past egui threshold, ghost follows cursor, folder hover validates target, release commits move/copy or cancels on blank/invalid.

D04.behavior: Existing egui drag threshold disambiguates click/select from drag. Clicks keep current selection/open behavior.

D05.behavior: Alt held at release copies; no Alt moves. Shift keeps rubber-band selection precedence. Ctrl is not an edit-drag modifier.

D06.behavior: No grid, ortho, or object snap applies to filesystem placement. The target is the deepest folder whose bounds contain the cursor, so a folder's whole rectangle accepts a drop — including over the files it already holds.

D07.behavior: n/a: filesystem drag has no direction or numeric parameter lock.

D08.behavior: n/a for drag. Rename and new-folder names are typed in the anchored popup; Enter commits, Esc cancels. Every edit-mode prompt and confirmation opens at the cursor, never at a screen edge.

D09.behavior: Drag paints a semi-transparent ghost at the cursor naming the destination folder (or saying the release does nothing) and highlights the valid folder target. The bottom readout shows running filesystem operation progress.

D10.behavior: Drag cursor is grabbing for move and copy cursor when Alt is held. Invalid/blank targets show no folder highlight.

D11.behavior: Release on valid folder dispatches a background FsOp. A copy is first accounted for cloud placeholders on a worker thread — files and whole folder subtrees, directory entries only — and confirms before downloading anything. Completed changes are journaled as FsRename, FsMove, FsCopy, or FsDelete and applied to the current index/tree.

D12.behavior: Release on blank canvas or invalid target is a null action: no filesystem operation, no dialog, no journal entry. Esc closes prompt/dialog layers before canvas state.

D13.behavior: Existing File Atlas selection presentation remains unchanged; edit drag does not add grips or bbox handles.

D14.behavior: Watcher/index reconciliation refreshes the canvas. Rename/move rewrite assignment keys so staged export metadata follows the file.

D15.behavior: No cut/paste file operations, no agent-initiated writes, and no Delete command outside Edit mode. Delete acts on the selection, or on the item under the cursor when nothing is selected — the only way to delete a folder from the keyboard, since folders are never part of a selection.

D16.behavior: n/a: filesystem operations do not inherit visual style.

D17.behavior: Picking up uses the card hit-test (`Tree::hit_test`); dropping uses containment (`Tree::dir_at_point`), because a drop is aimed at a folder, not at a card. The target rejects self, the current parent, and descendants of dragged folders.

D01.behavior: Command board.portal.web, board tabs only. Palette: "web portal" (aliases: embed, web page, iframe, url, dashboard, html). Portals dock flyout row. No single-key chord. Three drop-in entry paths create a bound portal at the pointer without arming a tool: dragging a browser tab or link out of Edge / Chrome / Firefox onto the board (the OLE payload carries UniformResourceLocatorW, text/uri-list, or CF_UNICODETEXT; atlas-core::shell_drag grows a URL arm beside its file arm); pasting an http(s) URL onto the board (Ctrl+V of clipboard text that parses as one); and dropping a .html/.htm file or a folder containing index.html, which makes a portal instead of a text card (Alt-drop keeps the text card, D05).

D02.behavior: P2.PortalPlace: one-shot, commit returns to Select, Space/Enter re-arms.

D03.behavior: P2.PortalPlace: Armed -> Dragging(rect) -> Committed(unbound), empty state "Choose page or file...", binding is a separate non-modal step (D19) - no file dialog and no network fetch inside a draw gesture. The three drop-in paths of D01 skip straight to Committed(bound).

D04.behavior: P2.PortalPlace: travel > draft.drag_threshold (4 px) uses the dragged rect; below it places portal.web.default_size (960x540) centred on the click.

D05.behavior: P2.PortalPlace Shift = 16:9. Addition: Alt while dropping a .html file bypasses the portal diversion and creates the legacy text snippet card. Ctrl unassigned in v1.

D06.behavior: P2.PortalPlace: grid snap and smart guides on the frame rect, never on contents.

D07.behavior: n/a - P2.PortalPlace has no directional parameter.

D08.behavior: No digit entry during placement. One numeric knob exists after commit and it is authored: viewport.width_css (default 1280), edited in the Portal inspector. Typed frame dimensions stay a non-goal (D15).

D09.behavior: During the drag: frame outline in Palette::portal + live w x h in the dock readout. Placed: a chrome strip carrying a globe glyph (URL) or file glyph (local), the display locator, the health dot (Ok/Unknown/Missing), and the poster capture age. A portal currently rendering live shows a small live dot in the strip; the one input-focused portal additionally gets a 2 px accent border, so "this is the frame holding my keyboard" is never ambiguous on a board where several are animating. Dock readout when selected: locator - source kind - viewport width - zoom mode - state.

D10.behavior: Crosshair while armed. Over a portal that is not input-focused - poster or live-rendering alike - the normal board arrow, because clicks select the frame. Over the input-focused portal, Slate applies the cursor the page requests through the composition controller. Over the chrome strip: always arrow, because the strip stays a Slate target.

D11.behavior: One journaled Add of PortalNode { class: Host, kind: Web, web: Some(WebPortalRef { source, entry, viewport, export_mode }) }. Poster texture, live state, scroll offset, and page history are derived and never journaled (Art. VI.3). One gesture = one undo. No style state consumed (D16).

D12.behavior: Esc peels one layer per press (P0.1): page input focus -> drag draft -> armed tool -> selection. Releasing input focus returns the portal to ordinary live rendering; it does not tear the webview down, and page state (scroll position, form contents, running charts) survives. Teardown happens only on pool eviction (D29) or node delete, and aborts any in-flight load.

D13.behavior: Standard frame handles (resize + rotation), joining the shared handle-carousel pattern. Contents expose no grips. Resize scales the rendered page (D20 zoom Fit); it does not reflow unless viewport is Auto. Rotation is fully supported: contents composite as a texture in the scene, so a rotated portal keeps rendering and stays hit-testable through its rotated rect, exactly like an image.

D14.behavior: Portal sidebar section when selected, mirrored by portal.web.* commands, each a journaled Patch: source (URL field / Choose file... / Choose folder + entry), viewport width and zoom mode, export mode, Reload, Recapture poster, Open in system browser, Package into workbook folder (Art. IX.4), and Allow this origin (local trust, not journaled - D32).

D15.behavior: Cut, each a decision (Art. III): browser chrome (tabs, back/forward, address bar, bookmarks, history), devtools, downloads, popups and window.open (blocked, offered as open-in-browser), printing, a cookie jar shared with the user's real browser, persisted logins across sessions, notifications / geolocation / camera / mic / clipboard-read, scraping page DOM into board nodes, writing back to the source HTML file (Art. IX.5), and typed frame dimensions (D08). Not cut, deferred to its own contract: the declared control surface of D18 - the only channel that will ever cross the frame boundary, carrying typed parameter values from Slate into the page. Arbitrary JS bridges, host objects, and page-initiated postMessage into Slate stay permanently cut. Page-internal navigation while focused is allowed but never persisted: the authored locator is the home.

D17.behavior: The frame picks on its (rotated) rect, including marquee, whenever it is not input-focused: a live-rendering portal is still an ordinary board node under the cursor. Only the single input-focused portal routes pointer and keyboard to the page and selects nothing on the board, and even then the chrome strip and a portal.web.border_hit_px (6 px) border band stay Slate targets so the frame can be grabbed and released. No board tool reaches the contents.

D18.behavior: Host, with one named future exception. The page owns its own runtime and Slate owns no mutations inside it; the only journaled acts are on the frame - place, move, resize, rebind, re-parameterize, delete, bake. The exception, deferred to its own contract: a hosted surface may declare a control surface of named, typed parameters, which board wires drive from other nodes - the case being a dashboard with sliders wired to an input node so other board content moves them. Values written that way are authored journaled data on the Slate side and travel one way, Slate -> page, over a declarative typed channel; the page never issues commands back, which keeps Art. VII.3 (data, not code) and VII.4 intact and makes the exception explicit rather than accidental. Determinism is not required of host portals (P1.portal.determinism).

D19.behavior: SourceUri.locator holds exactly one of: an http(s) URL; a path to an .html/.htm file; or a path to a directory plus WebPortalRef.entry (default index.html) for a multi-file dashboard. Paths are relative to the workbook first, absolute as fallback (Art. IX.2). Bound by the inspector, the empty-state button, or by dropping a file/folder/tab on an unbound portal; rebinding is a journaled Patch that discards the cached poster. Refused: javascript: and data: URIs, non-http(s) schemes (ftp:, about:, custom protocol handlers), .slate files (diverted to open as a tab), and non-HTML files (which stay ordinary board items).

D20.behavior: Journaled: viewport.width_css (default 1280) - the CSS width the page is laid out at; viewport.zoom = Fit (scale the render to the frame width, default) | Fixed(f32) | Auto (frame size drives the CSS viewport, so resize reflows like a browser window); entry (folder sources); interactive_allowed (default true); poster_capture = OnBind | Manual (never a timer in v1); export_mode (D24); title; frame rect and fill. Derived: scroll offset, page history, live state, poster texture, load errors.

D21.behavior: Poster recapture triggers: bind/rebind, viewport change, explicit portal.web.recapture, pool eviction (D29), and - for local file/folder sources only - an mtime change found by a worker-thread poll no more often than portal.web.poll_secs (1.0). Remote URLs never auto-recapture: a network fetch is never implicit. Capture runs off-thread, generation-tagged; a stale capture is discarded, never painted (Art. II.3). While capturing, the previous poster stays at portal.web.stale_alpha (0.6) with a progress strip. Source gone: Missing, last poster retained and dimmed, locator named (P1.portal.health).

D22.behavior: Many render, one listens. Every pooled portal (D29) renders live all the time - charts tick, animations run - while pointer and keyboard stay with the board. Hover shows the full locator; single click selects the frame; double-click (or Enter on the selection) takes input focus, routing pointer and keyboard to that one page and marking it (D09); Esc or clicking elsewhere releases focus without stopping its rendering. Ctrl+double-click opens the locator in the system browser instead. While input-focused the wheel scrolls the page and Ctrl+wheel still zooms the camera, so P0.5 holds - flagged as a deviation because the plain wheel is surrendered for that one frame.

D23.behavior: Buckets key on the portal's on-screen height in physical pixels, so a hundred tiled pages zoomed out cost nothing. Below portal.web.lod_strip_px (96): chrome strip only, no texture bound. From 96 to portal.web.live_min_px (320), or off-screen at any size: the cached poster. At or above 320 and on screen: eligible for the live pool, admitted by the D29 priority; an eligible portal that misses admission paints its poster and reports Budgeted. Double-clicking a portal below the live threshold zooms the camera to fit it first, then takes input focus, rather than refusing.

D24.behavior: Two modes, journaled per portal, defaulting by source kind (OQ2 = A). Local file/folder: packaged iframe - build_assets copies the entry file and its folder into assets/ and rewrites the locator (Art. IX.4 fork, origin recorded in the manifest), and the writer emits

D25.behavior: portal.web.bake emits one journaled Add batch: an Image node holding the captured poster (written into the workbook assets) plus a provenance Text node naming the locator, the source kind, and the capture time. The portal is left in place - bake copies, it does not convert. Exact repo-lens D25 precedent.

D26.behavior: Frame, locator, entry, viewport, and export mode sync as ordinary journal deltas. Poster texture, live/pool state, scroll offset, page history, and per-origin consent are per-peer and never transmitted - each peer runs its own pool, and only the peer who focuses a portal gives it input. A peer that cannot resolve the locator paints Unknown naming the locator it tried (P1.portal.health). Consent is deliberately not journaled: a .slate you received must never arrive carrying someone else's decision to trust a host.

D27.behavior: Parity, mediated by the existing autonomy grant. Agents and humans drive the identical board.portal.web / portal.web.* commands with identical privileges (Art. VII.1); agent-issued mutations stage for acceptance by default and apply directly where the workspace has granted autonomy (Art. VII.6) - the same rule that governs every command, not a portal-specific leash. Origin consent (D32) is a command like any other and follows that same path. The remaining restrictions are capability-level, not agent-level: nobody, human or agent, can read page DOM, cookies, or storage, or make the page issue a command, because no such channel exists (D15). Art. IX.5's "never available to an agent" clause governs write-back to sources and does not bite here - this portal never writes to its source. The context beacon carries locator, source kind, viewport, and state.

D28.behavior: n/a - P1.portal.determinism: determinism is required of generated portals only (Art. V.3), and Art. IV.2 governs extracted graphs; neither describes a hosted page. What this portal owes instead is provenance, shown on the frame and in every export: resolved locator, source kind, content hash (local) or capture timestamp (remote), viewport width, and the origin recorded by packaging.

D29.behavior: A pool, not a webview per page. At most portal.web.live_pool (6) webviews exist at once, admitted from the eligible set (D23) by priority: input-focused first, then greatest on-screen area, then most recently focused. Eviction captures a poster on the way out, so a demoted portal degrades to its last frame rather than blanking. Contents composite offscreen into a texture (WebView2 visual hosting), so portals obey z-order, rotation, and opacity like any node. Frame rates are budgeted, not free: the input-focused portal renders at the board's rate, other pooled portals at portal.web.idle_fps (5), and texture uploads are capped at portal.web.uploads_per_frame (2) per frame with the remainder held in a backlog that requests a repaint - the per-frame-budget rule the scanner and watcher already follow. Poster capture is async and generation-tagged; posters cache by (locator, content hash or capture epoch, viewport width) and evict with the thumbnail tier (Art. II.2). Nothing on the frame loop touches the network or the filesystem; the local mtime poll is a worker at >= 1 s. The research-hub case is therefore a hundred cached textures, at most six processes, and none at all once the board zooms past the strip threshold. A missing WebView2 runtime degrades every portal to NoRuntime, never a stall.

D30.behavior: Unbound ("Choose page or file..."). Unknown - not yet resolved, neutral marker, never blocking (P1.portal.health). Blocked - remote origin not yet permitted, host named. Loading. Live. Budgeted - eligible but outside the live pool, showing its last frame and saying so. Poster(age) - stale by construction, age stated. Missing - file gone, DNS failure, or 404, locator named, last poster kept. Refused(reason) - unsupported or dangerous scheme. NoRuntime - WebView2 runtime absent, with what to install. TooSmall - below live_min_px. NotFramable - export-time note when a remote site refuses iframing. Every state names itself in the frame rather than blanking it.

D31.behavior: Journaled authored intent: frame rect / rotation / opacity / fill, title, locator, entry, viewport width and zoom mode, interactive_allowed, poster_capture mode, export mode. Derived per-peer: poster texture and its capture time, live/pool membership, input focus, scroll offset, page navigation history, load errors, origin consent grants, WebView2 runtime availability.

D32.behavior: Remote origins are Blocked until the human permits them; grants key on (workbook, origin), live in local app state, and are never journaled or written into the .slate, so a workbook you receive cannot arrive pre-trusting a host. Local sources under the workbook root need no prompt. The webview runs in a per-workbook user-data folder - no cookies, storage, or logins shared with the user's real browser. Denied outright: downloads, popups, notifications, geolocation, camera, microphone, clipboard read, and any host object or postMessage bridge (D15). Exports sandbox what they embed: packaged local content gets sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin", because a dashboard must fetch its own sibling data files; remote iframes get allow-scripts only.
